messages.subject: cbs_error_in_250k_sty_cn_analysis_
parts:
Hi All

I am analyzing 250k sty samples (only) (paired: healthy Vs tumor). No.
of samples around 72 (36 each, paired). I am following the tutorial
posted on http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/paired-total-copy-number-analysis.
Till identification of copy-number regions in tumor-normal pairs,
tutorial works for me. But at cbsmodel, analysis fails. Following is
the error message:

===================
> cns <- CbsModel(sets$tumor, sets$normal);
Error in max(lens, length(allNames)) : invalid 'type' (list) of
argument

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.9.1 (2009-06-26)
i386-pc-mingw32

locale:
LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252;LC_CTYPE=English_United States.
1252;LC_MONETARY=English_United States.
1252;LC_NUMERIC=C;LC_TIME=English_United States.1252

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods
base

other attached packages:
[1] DNAcopy_1.18.0 aroma.affymetrix_1.1.2
aroma.apd_0.1.6 affxparser_1.16.0 R.huge_0.1.8
[6] aroma.core_1.1.4 aroma.light_1.12.2
matrixStats_0.1.7 R.rsp_0.3.5 R.filesets_0.5.3
[11] digest_0.3.1 R.cache_0.1.8
R.utils_1.1.7 R.oo_1.4.9 R.methodsS3_1.0.3

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_2.9.1
=================================================

I am sure that I am making a small mistake. What I have done is as
follows:

1) I loaded the cel files as per the instructions.
2) pairs files was externally supplied and converted into matrix
3) raw cel files are properly defined using following commands:
===================
csRawList <- list();
for (chipType in chipTypes) {
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName(dataSetName, chipType=chipType);
stopifnot(all(getNames(cs) %in% pairs));
csRawList[[chipType]] <- cs;
}

print(csRawList)
==============

every thing works out well so far.

4) I follow the work flow till Identificaiton of copy-number regions
in tumor-normal pairs and works well till

==========# Split data set in (tumor, normal) pairs
sets <- list(tumor=list(), normal=list());
for (chipType in names(cesFlnList)) {
ces <- cesFlnList[[chipType]];
for (type in colnames(pairs)) {
idxs <- match(pairs[,type], getNames(ces));
sets[[type]][[chipType]] <- extract(ces, idxs);
}
}
========

5) and fails here : cns <- CbsModel(sets$tumor, sets$normal);

I guess here is where the problem lies: in defining the sets. I am not
sure how to do that.

Can some one help me ?

suresh

parts:
Hi Henrik

Thanks for the reply. I was able to troubleshoot the problem. I was
analyzing sty chips and in chip types, I included both the chips (sty
and nsp). Since there are no corresponding cel files (nsp), it was
generating lists with null values. Once i sorted that out, every thing
worked like charm.

An unrelated question: Is cbsmodel is the same as that (cbs)
implemented in DNAcopy ? From the loaded packages, I can see DNAcopy
package. When i ran DNAcopy independently (by supplying values
externally in a tsv), on the same samples that I used in aroma
affymetrix, for segmentaion, CBS (in DNAcopy) took forever (more than
48 hours).

Regards

suresh
